findings.title: Google Meet fallback crashes when destinationCalendar is empty
findings.body: create() now reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without a null check. If destinationCalendar is missing or [], destructuring yields undefined and this throws before any calendar or video event is created. Previously optional chaining treated a missing calendar as not Google and fell back to Cal Video. Bookings that use Google Meet with no destination calendar now fail entirely instead of falling back.

findings.title: Collective host calendars dropped when organizer has none
findings.body: Team destination calendars are appended with evt.destinationCalendar?.push. When neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, the field is set to null, so the push is skipped and teamDestinationCalendars is discarded. Collective hosts who do have calendars connected never get events created, which is the case this PR is meant to fix.

findings.title: Office 365 always writes the first host's calendar
findings.body: createEvent ignores the credentialId now passed by EventManager and always uses destinationCalendar[0].externalId. For a collective booking, EventManager calls createEvent once per host credential, but every call targets the main host's calendar id. Secondary hosts' tokens then hit the wrong calendar (create fails) and their own calendars never receive the event. LarkCalendarService has the same [0]-only behavior in create/update/delete.

findings.title: Organizer email is always the first destination calendar
findings.body: createEvent inserts into the calendar matching credentialId, but the organizer attendee email is always destinationCalendar[0].externalId. On a secondary host's calendar that external id is a different Google account, so the insert can be rejected or stored with the wrong organizer. updateEvent repeats the same mistake, so reschedules rewrite every host's copy with the first host's email.

findings.title: Update/delete calendar fallback never matches
findings.body: When externalCalendarId is missing, updateEvent and deleteEvent search destinationCalendar for an entry whose externalId equals that same missing value, which cannot match. The old code fell back to destinationCalendar.externalId. Updates now call Google with an undefined calendarId and fail; deletes only survive because they default to "primary", which may be the wrong calendar. Any booking reference without externalCalendarId can no longer be updated.

findings.title: Recurring cancel deletes the wrong events, repeatedly
findings.body: The new per-reference loop still runs the recurring branch inside each reference. That branch loads every calendar credential on the booking owner and, for every remaining instance, deletes only references.find("_calendar") — the first calendar reference — not the reference currently being processed. Extra host events are never deleted, and the same first event id is deleted once per reference times every calendar credential, producing duplicate failing API calls and leaving other hosts' recurring events on their calendars.

findings.title: Paid confirmation only creates the organizer calendar event
findings.body: Payment success rebuilds CalendarEvent from booking.destinationCalendar or the booking owner's destination calendar only, then calls EventManager.create. Booking stores a single destinationCalendar relation (handleNewBooking connects [0]), so collective host calendars gathered at booking time are gone. Stripe's payment webhook does the same. Paid collective bookings therefore confirm with a calendar event for one host only.

findings.title: Organization slug condition is inverted
findings.body: Unrelated to destination calendars, the create payload changed from setting slug when team billing is disabled to setting slug only when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true. Self-hosted orgs no longer get a slug, and billing-enabled orgs now persist slug immediately instead of only requestedSlug. Organization URLs will be wrong or rejected after create.
